item.title: PostDoc Biomarker (m/f/d)
item.description: Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung, Frankfurt a. M. Bewerbungsende: 24.08.2026 | The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level. The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity and climate change. We are looking for an organic biomarker expert with proven experience in deep time paleoclimate research. We strive to explore material from UNESCO World Heritage sites and experience in handling material from such environments is desired. One key goal of the position is to contribute to the reconstruction of highly-resolved deep-time paleoclimate records in Central Europe during a key climate interval of the Paleogene. Ihre Aufgaben Using state-of-the-art biomarker analytics to develop a paleoclimatic framework within a highly-resolved deep-time paleoclimate archive Contribute to refinement of biomarker proxy applications General contributions to laboratory development Collaborate with geologists and paleobiologists in the team to establish interrelationships between climatic change and paleo biological diversity Ihr Profil Doctoral degree in Earth Sciences with particular focus on organic biomarker geochemistry in deep time paleoclimate archives Profound and documented experience in stable isotope geochemistry and biomarker analysis Expertise in data analysis and willingness to collaborate closely with colleagues in paleobiology, paleoclimate research and Earth surface processes Proven ability to publish biomarker geochemistry data in scientific journals with highest scientific standards Profound experience in organic geochemical laboratory work Excellent written and oral communication skills in German and English Research experience in interdisciplinary working environments (desirable) Unser Angebot opportunity to work closely with leading experts in Earth System Research as well as paleoenvironmental reconstructions access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture. Ihre Bewerbung Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) (as a single PDF) by 24.08.2026. Contact Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung Senckenberganlage 25 60325 Frankfurt am Main For specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Andreas Mulch at andreas.mulch@senckenberg.de For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung. zur Stellenausschreibung Achtung! item.title: Semantic Backend Developer (f/m/d) – Hamburg
item.description: Leibniz-Institut zur Analyse des Biodiversitätswandels (LIB), Hamburg Bewerbungsende: 31.08.2026 | The Leibniz Institute for the Analysis of Biodiversity Change (LIB) is one of the large, globally connected research museums of the Leibniz Association. In addition to excellent research on biodiversity and its change, we are advancing the further development of our extensive scientific collections with an international team and state-of-the-art technology. With our exhibition, knowledge transfer and communication work at our exhibition venues Museum Koenig Bonn and Museum der Natur Hamburg, we want to spread enthusiasm for nature and contribute with our research topics to current socio-political discussions on species loss, climate change and the protection of ecosystems. The construction of an integrated natural history museum is being planned for the Hamburg location; the research infrastructure at the Bonn location is currently being significantly expanded. The LIB Centre for Biodiversity Knowledge Science is developing the LIB Open Knowledge Space, a FAIR and CLEAR, modular, and service-oriented system that is based on formal semantics and RDF/OWL knowledge graphs. It will contain all research-project and collection-based data and knowledge of the LIB, and will strengthen curatorial and scientific work by providing tools and infrastructures that make biodiversity data and knowledge publishable, citable, and reusable without compromising ownership or expertise. Each component of the underlying infrastructure provides its own API and can evolve independently, with adapters mediating between services following principles such as Hexagonal Architecture. By linking collections, research, and communication through advanced data and knowledge science, semantic technologies, and artificial intelligence, the LIB Open Knowledge Space will enable the LIB to function as a globally connected and future-ready, open biodiversity knowledge hub, while preserving scientific authority and institutional responsibility. Become part of our institute in Hamburg. We are looking for the next possible date, limited according to the part-time and fixed-term law for 2 years (with the possibility of permanent employment) a Semantic Backend Developer (f/m/d) – Hamburg in full-time 39.00 hours/week Your tasks: • Contribute to shaping the architecture of the LIB Open Knowledge Space (LIB-OKS). • Development of the semantic backend (database infrastructure) of the LIB-OKS and implementation of interfaces and program logic for the provision and curation of data from the LIB-OKS. • Contribution to the design and implementation of front-end views for the presentation and curation of the LIB-OKS. • Integration of existing databases into the LIB-OKS. • Act as a technical gatekeeper for production systems: Ensure that emerging solutions meet high standards of: Quality, Sustainability, Interoperability and ensure compliance with the FAIR and CLEAR Principles. • Support agile prototype development. • Contribute to the development of national and international networks for biodiversity research and knowledge science (e.g., NFDI, DiSSCo, TDWG). • Assist in securing external funding for research projects. • Enable the reuse of software components by the wider biodiversity and research infrastructure community. Your profile: • Strong expertise in knowledge graphs and semantic technologies. • Ability to design conceptual and technical architectures for complex knowledge structures, including hybrid solutions combining semantic technologies, classical databases, and AI-mediated representations. • Strong backend programming and software development skills in languages such as Python, Java, Kotlin, or Scala, including clean, modular, tested, and well-documented code. • Experience designing maintainable, modular, service-oriented or event-driven systems, including APIs, versioning, service integration patterns, and interoperability across heterogeneous tools. • Experience with data ingestion, transformation, and validation pipelines using technologies such as SHACL or LinkML. • Familiarity with FAIR data principles and related approaches, including Linked Data, persistent identifiers, FAIR Digital Objects, Nanopublications, and RO-Crates. • Knowledge of biodiversity informatics, life sciences data, or museum/collection data. • Strong communication skills for working with researchers, curators, data scientists, software developers. • Experience in applying for third-party funding (national and international). • Experience in networking on national and international levels and contributing to long-term projects and goals. • Proven publication record and/or proven track of software contributions or maintained code repositories. We offer: • An attractive position in an excellent research institution with a high degree of creative potential in a dynamic scientific and social environment • Remuneration according to the collective agreement of the federal states (up to EG 13 TV-L if the personal and job-related requirements of the collective agreement are met) with all the benefits of the public sector (company pension scheme, annual special payment, capital-forming benefits, collectively agreed vacation entitlement) • Family friendliness certified by the “Work and Family Audit”, offer of life coaching through professional family service • the possibility of obtaining a job ticket • A centrally located workplace with excellent transport links Please send your complete application documents (including cover letter, CV, copies of certificates, max. 10 MB) by 31.08.2026 exclusively digitally via our career portal to Ms. Winkels: https://8101202752.karriereportal.cloud/ For organizational reasons, only online applications will be accepted. We are a diverse institution and welcome our diversity. We would particularly like to encourage women to apply in order to actively promote equal opportunities. Severely disabled people will be given preference if equally qualified. item.description: Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA), Schleswig Bewerbungsende: 25.08.2026 | Das Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA), Mitglied der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft, ist ein weltweit tätiges archäologisches Forschungsinstitut und Museum mit Hauptsitz in Mainz und weiteren Standorten in Neuwied, Mayen und Schleswig. Seit seiner Gründung im Jahr 1852 widmet sich das Museum den materiellen Hinterlassenschaften aus drei Millionen Jahren Menschheitsgeschichte mit dem Ziel, menschliches Verhalten und Handeln sowie die Entwicklung und den Wandel von Gesellschaften zu verstehen. Für den Standort Schleswig suchen wir schnellstmöglich eine*n Post-Doktorand*in (m/w/d) in der Prähistorischen Archäologie (EG 13 TV-L) in Vollzeit, befristet für 15 Monate. Während des späten Pleistozäns und frühen Holozäns war Nordeuropa von mobilen Jägern und Sammlern bevölkert. Aufgrund ihres nicht sesshaften Lebensstils sind Spuren dieser Gesellschaften schwer zu finden, was unser Verständnis ihrer Lebensweise und Entwicklung erschwert. Einige Teile der südwestlichen Ostsee wurden jedoch erst im Holozän überflutet und könnten daher anthropogene Strukturen und Landschaften aus dieser paläolithischen/frühen mesolithischen Zeit enthalten. Kürzlich wurde in der südwestlichen Ostsee eine versunkene Steinmauer entdeckt, die wahrscheinlich aus der Steinzeit stammt und für die Jagd genutzt wurde. Ähnliche Jagdstrukturen, welche offenbar der Massenjagd auf Huftierherden dienten, wurden auch an anderen Orten der Welt gefunden. Ein dreijähriges Projekt (SEASCAPE), gefördert von der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft, zielt darauf ab, diese Struktur detaillierter zu verstehen, andere bisher unbekannte steinzeitliche Megastrukturen am Ostseeboden zu identifizieren und die Paläoumweltbedingungen zu rekonstruieren, unter denen diese Strukturen errichtet wurden. Am Projekt SEASCAPE sind auf den Gebieten der Archäologie, Geologie, Geophysik und Paläoklimatologie wissenschaftlich tätige Personen des Leibniz-Instituts für Ostseeforschung Warnemünde (IOW), des Leibniz-Zentrums für Archäologie, Standort Schleswig (LEIZA), der Universität Rostock und der Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel beteiligt. Im Rahmen des SEASCAPE-Projekts ist der LEIZA-Kompetenzbereich 1 „Pleistozäne und Frühholozäne Archäologie“ am Standort Schleswig im Arbeitspaket 1 für die Suche nach gemeinsamen globalen Merkmalen solcher Strukturen verantwortlich, die für deren Funktion entscheidend sind.
